frames.narration: One thread, the event loop, runs both handlers. It takes one ready task at a time and runs it until it finishes or awaits. Waiting on I/O happens outside the thread.
Handler A reads the shared counter (0), then awaits a database call. At the await it leaves the loop. The loop is free to run something else.
The loop runs Handler B. B also reads the counter, and it is still 0. Then it awaits too.
Both calls finish. A resumes and writes 1, then B resumes and writes 1. One thread, no two steps mixed, and an update is still lost: the gap was the await.
Now a CPU-heavy request: Handler A calculates for 40 ticks and never awaits. The loop is stuck on it. A health-check ping arrives and waits in the queue.
Option 1: send the calculation to a worker thread. The loop stays free, so the ping and other requests are served at once, and A continues when the worker is done.
Option 2: slice the work into pieces of 5 ticks that go back to the queue. The ping gets in after one slice, but every request now finishes later, because they share the loop.
